data.text: Operator 2026-11-11 answers. Workflow profile: user highest, a company floor is a default (a person-only local override may loosen it, recorded and visible); strict-delivery profile opt-in at onboarding; operator disposal of review findings by chat approval is enough; final review round = strongest reviewer on the full diff only above a size/risk threshold (configurable). Rename the new WP- tasks to WFP-. Accept all six proposed decisions: D-merge-smoke-gate, D-approval-recipe-list, D-pin-refresh-owner, D-lease-lifecycle-automation, D-phase-needs-scope, D-accepted-baseline-red. Phase needs: phase-level only unless a task opts in (needs_apply = phase default). Merge smoke gate: when a needed tool is missing record unavailable (never passed) and continue (NOT refuse). Revive the abandoned affected-tests scope as TS-impact-select gated on TS-impact-probe. Toolkit ideas to file: deviation record + citation check, commitments tier (AFTER GP-waiver lands: file it with a need on GP-waiver), readiness-audit gate, company baseline importer (patterns only, runtime import, copies nothing); also all six of: effort-adjustment rules as a layered table, one source emitted per harness, pack lint for imported skills, prose-gate recipe as documentation, a doctor view of what loads per request with a budget knob, a model-comparison log kind. The work-item (tracker) adapter folds under CP-intake and IA-forge.

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-merge-smoke-gate-2026-11-11 as written, with one change: [smoke].on_unavailable defaults to 'unavailable'. When a tool the smoke gate needs (ruff, bandit, an import probe target) is missing or cannot run, that check is recorded unavailable (never counted as passed) and the gate continues with the remaining checks; it does NOT refuse the merge. 'refuse' stays a configurable value of on_unavailable. A check that ran and failed still refuses the merge and never starts the full suite. Everything else (budget_s 60, derived module list, full suite once per main commit, red main priority) is as in the superseded record.
data.title: Merge smoke gate accepted: a missing needed tool records unavailable and the gate continues

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-phase-needs-scope-2026-11-11 with this answer: phase needs apply at the phase level only unless a task opts in. needs_apply defaults to 'phase' (the phase itself cannot start or close until its needs are done; its tasks do not inherit). A phase or a task opts into inheritance with an explicit inherit flag (needs_apply = tasks on the phase, or inherit = true on a task). 'ddflow phase lift <id> --need <id> --reason ...' is the one-command audited lift: it removes one edge with a recorded decision, an event and a doctor entry listing active lifts. Existing phases keep their historical behaviour until migrated, with a migration note and a doctor list of phases whose tasks inherit.
data.title: Phase needs scope accepted: phase-level unless a task opts in

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-wp-profile-shape-r2 with answers: (1) the user layer is highest; a company floor is a default, and a person-only local override may loosen it, recorded and visible (consistent with D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06). (2) The strict-delivery profile is opt-in at onboarding; the shipped default stays the existing default profile. Everything else (one layered declarative record, shipped < company < project < user, stages as data over existing gates, approvals and review config, no second engine) is as in the superseded record.
data.title: Workflow profile shape accepted: user highest, company floor is a default, strict-delivery opt-in

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-wp-review-ladder-disposal with answers: (1) operator disposal of review findings by chat approval is enough (dispose_by = operator is a person-only chat approval, no extra ceremony). (2) The final round (strongest enabled reviewer on the full diff) runs only above a size/risk threshold, configurable as [review].final_round_min_lines and a risk predicate; below it the cheap-round ladder ends the review. Everything else (rounds as data, advisory mode, bounded caps) is as in the superseded record.
data.title: Review ladder accepted: operator disposal by chat approval, final strongest round above a threshold

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-wp-route-predicate as written; per-item profile binding follows the operator's answers on D-wp-profile-shape-r2-accepted (user highest, strict-delivery opt-in at onboarding).
data.title: Item routing predicate accepted

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-runs-per-merge as written: ddflow metrics reports first-pass gate rate and gate re-runs per merged item (per item, phase, model); a [bounded] knob stops an item after N failed runs and asks the operator; deterministic and model gates are labelled separately. Reuses gate records; no new events.
data.title: Runs to merge accepted as a first-class metric with a stop-after-N-failures knob

data.body: Declares the diagram's stages as profile data over existing gates, approvals and review config; also registers the 'light' (extends UX-light-profile) and 'bugfix' catalogue entries by name. Tighten-only versus company floors per LF-profile. Acceptance: ddflow flow profile show strict-delivery prints every stage, pipeline, checkpoint and round cap; a test that loads the shipped template and fails before the template exists; a user-layer copy overrides one stage without touching the shipped file. Estimated size: M (about 250 lines). CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows, r-bounded-everything, r-reuse-core, D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06, D-wp-profile-shape-r2): every number, list and mode is a knob in the named [section], settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, in the layers shipped < company < project < user, defaults shipped as overridable templates, no hard-coded constants; README knob-table row and upgrade fragment per the repo conventions; a tool or reviewer that could not run is unavailable, never passed. Source: R-workflow-profile-2026-11-11 (operator request 2026-11-11: could ddflow support the gsms-style delivery workflow, with configuration).

data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 accepts D-prompt-layers as written: always-on text is ordered by change frequency: L0 static (charter, MCP contract), L1 slow (rules, decisions, project facts), L2 per task (body, acceptance), L3 per turn (brief, resume, last gate). No counts, timestamps or per-session state in L0/L1; doctor lints it and measures cache hit from usage; the volatile handshake lines move to the brief.
data.title: Always-on text layers L0-L3 accepted: change-frequency order and a byte-stable handshake

data.body: Evaluated at task add and on update through the guidance predicate engine over existing fields plus the GV-complexity-score; yes routes the item through the capability-brief stage, no skips it. [lifecycle].routes is an ordered list of {when, profile, stage_skip}; the result is an event carrying the reason, and a person may override. No classifier model by default.
